open_points.subject: A17 rule 1 path-component failure
open_points.text: a component that cannot be opened so, for whatever reason, making the file one that cannot be read —, and the checks and the read use that one opened file
open_points.question: What exact outcome follows when any path component cannot be opened with the required flags, and does the same rule classify configuration-file and credential-file failures according to their respective contexts?
options: The configuration path refuses startup, while a credential path yields credential_unresolved
Every component-opening failure refuses startup
Use the underlying operating-system error
open_points.default_guess: Treat the file as unreadable: refuse startup for the configuration file and return credential_unresolved for a credential file.

open_points.subject: A17/A20 O_NOFOLLOW support boundary
open_points.text: each component with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW`, whose presence no code tests (A20 rule 3)
open_points.question: What exactly counts as a supported host having O_NOFOLLOW: exposure of the constant by CPython, acceptance by the running kernel, or enforcement by the filesystem for every opened component?
options: CPython exposes os.O_NOFOLLOW
The running kernel accepts the flag
The kernel and every relevant filesystem enforce no-follow semantics
open_points.default_guess: Require the CPython constant and rely on Linux and the filesystem to enforce its documented no-follow semantics.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 1 exclusive data-directory lock
open_points.text: At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory; a second process on the same directory refuses to start.
open_points.question: What lock object and locking mechanism define ownership of the data directory, and how are stale lock artifacts, unsupported locking, and other lock-acquisition errors handled?
options: Use a persistent lock file with an OS advisory lock that is released on process death
Use an atomically created marker file and remove it on shutdown
Lock the SQLite database itself
open_points.default_guess: Open a fixed lock file without following links, take a nonblocking OS advisory exclusive lock for the process lifetime, and refuse startup on every acquisition error.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 2 private data-directory tree
open_points.text: The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
open_points.question: Which ownership, permission, and file-type checks make the directory and every existing entry "private," including directories, regular files, the configured data-directory path itself, and special or hard-linked files?
options: Require ownership by the effective kernel user and no group/other permission bits on every entry
Require only that group and others cannot read entries
Apply the explicit A17 regular-file ownership and mode rule to files and an analogous searchable-directory rule to directories
open_points.default_guess: Require the data directory and every entry to be owned by the effective kernel user with no group or other permission bits, and refuse unexpected special files.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 2 data-directory symlink scope
open_points.text: Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links; a link found at start stops the start
open_points.question: Does the symlink prohibition also cover the configured data-directory path and every component leading to it, or only entries located below the resolved directory?
options: Reject symlinks in the data-directory path and anywhere below it
Reject only symlink entries below the resolved data directory
Reject only symlinks encountered when opening a particular store object
open_points.default_guess: Reject symlinks in the data-directory path and throughout its managed tree.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 3 request serialization
open_points.text: Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive
open_points.question: What event establishes arrival order when requests are received concurrently on different MCP connections or tasks?
options: Order when the complete request message has been received
Order when transport handling begins
Order by acquisition of the single request mutex
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonic queue position when each complete request has been received and process those positions in order.

open_points.subject: A18 store record order
open_points.text: The kernel is one process with one store and one writer.
open_points.question: How is the single store order assigned when one transaction creates or changes several records, and do updates to mutable entities keep their original position or obtain a new position?
options: Every created record receives a distinct sequence in an explicitly specified write order; updates keep the original position
All records in one transaction share one position with a secondary order
Every insert and update receives a new store position
open_points.default_guess: Give each newly created record a distinct monotonically increasing sequence in the store call's specified write order, while updates retain the entity's creation position.

open_points.subject: A18 rules 3–4 database/file crash consistency
open_points.text: Value bytes and spooled files are written to a temporary file, flushed, checked against their digest and size, and then renamed into place; a completed file a record names is never overwritten
open_points.question: What commit and durability ordering guarantees that a crash cannot leave a committed record naming a missing or non-durable file, and what must startup do if such a record is nevertheless found?
options: Publish and durably sync the file and directory before committing the database record; refuse startup on a missing or corrupt referenced file
Commit the database first and repair missing files during recovery
Permit records whose payload file was lost and fail only when the payload is read
open_points.default_guess: Durably publish and sync the file before committing its referencing record, and refuse startup if a referenced file is missing or fails digest and size verification.

open_points.subject: A18 content-addressed file collision handling
open_points.question: What happens when the target digest path already exists but its bytes or size differ from the bytes now being published under the same digest?
options: Verify the existing file and fail the store call on any mismatch
Assume digest equality proves byte equality and reuse it without reading
Publish under a secondary collision identity
open_points.default_guess: Verify the existing file's size and digest, reuse it only when equal, and otherwise fail the store call as an integrity error without overwriting it.

open_points.subject: A18 orphan fixture and spool cleanup
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... and the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool ... are removed; nothing else is.
open_points.question: What happens to an unreferenced trial fixture or a spool directory whose run record was never committed after a failed store call, given that K-10 permits only trial-case fixtures beyond runs and A18 says nothing else is removed?
options: Remove every unreferenced fixture and every spool directory with no live run record at startup
Keep them forever because rule 4 says nothing else is removed
Prevent such fixture or spool orphans by a separate atomic publication protocol
open_points.default_guess: Remove unreferenced fixture files and spool directories that have no corresponding run record during startup recovery.
